name: Unicorn Platform
tagline: Assemble a startup landing page from constrained components and export static code

tiers.name: Lurker
tiers.limits: 0 published websites; up to 10 pages and 10 blog posts in the builder; 10 AI uses; no custom domain, code export or collaborators
tiers.notes: Free forever for drafting, but it does not include a live published site.

tiers.name: Maker
tiers.limits: 1 published website; unlimited pages; 10 blog posts; custom domain and code export; 0 collaborators; Unicorn branding remains

tiers.name: Startup
tiers.limits: 1 published website; unlimited pages and blog posts; 1 collaborator; branding removal; custom domain and code export

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 3 published websites; unlimited pages, blog posts and collaborators; branding removal and code export

tiers.name: Freelancer
tiers.limits: 8 published websites; unlimited pages, blog posts and collaborators; branding removal and code export

tiers.name: Agency
tiers.limits: 20 published websites; unlimited pages, blog posts and collaborators; branding removal and code export

tiers.name: Major
tiers.limits: 100 published websites; unlimited pages, blog posts and collaborators; branding removal and code export

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 pages, 10 blog posts and 10 AI uses, but 0 published websites; no custom domain, export, collaborators or branding removal
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (live table discounts vary by tier, roughly 29% to 40%); 30-day money-back guarantee on paid plans
pricing.hiddenCosts: Custom domains are bought separately; Stripe/payment-processing charges and fees from connected third-party services are not included

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Unicorn Platform, assemble a startup landing page from constrained components and export static code. The hard boundary is template polish, hosted publishing, forms, and ai copy convenience, plus editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem.
coreLoopDIY: Assemble a startup landing page from constrained components, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and export static code or publish to a user-owned target.
whatYouLose: template polish, hosted publishing, forms, and AI copy convenience
moatNotes: editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem
ongoingBurden: responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Unicorn Platform because the page renderer is reproducible, but customers pay to avoid becoming their own hosting and browser-compatibility team. The recurring cost buys responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Webstudio
priorArt.desc: Open-source visual website builder designed around web standards.

alternatives.name: Mobirise AI
alternatives.desc: Block-based startup sites with code export and three free projects a month.

facts.install: Browser signup; projects can be hosted by Mobirise or exported as HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.engines: Proprietary text-to-site, copy, image and video generation; the underlying model providers are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Projects are saved in the hosted builder; export downloads ordinary HTML, CSS, JavaScript and asset files
facts.gapVsPaid: Mobirise AI lacks Unicorn Platform's startup-specific copy and conversion defaults, and the free generator is capped at three sites per month.
facts.setupBlocker: The permanent free allowance is capped at three distinct generated/exported projects per month

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: Reusable components, hosting and code deployment on a free plan; much less constrained than requested.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional npm-installed Plasmic CLI for React code generation and deployment in your own repository
facts.engines: Plasmic AI (beta); the official site does not name its underlying model provider
facts.dataFormat: Hosted projects and CMS records in Plasmic Cloud; codegen writes React components plus plasmic.json and plasmic.lock into the user's repository
facts.gapVsPaid: Plasmic lacks Unicorn Platform's constrained startup copy, pricing, testimonial and lead-capture workflow, trading speed for control.
facts.setupBlocker: Free hosted output keeps Plasmic branding; codegen/self-deployment requires a Node/React project and deployment workflow

alternatives.name: Publii
alternatives.desc: A desktop block editor that exports a static site; startup-specific components are not the main attraction.

facts.install: Install the native Windows/macOS package or Linux AppImage
facts.dataFormat: Source content and media in a user-selected local Sites Location; publishing generates static HTML, CSS and assets, with optional local backup archives
facts.gapVsPaid: Publii lacks startup-specific sections, lead-capture defaults and instant hosted publishing.
facts.setupBlocker: Publishing still needs separate hosting plus SFTP, GitHub or Netlify credentials/configuration

alternatives.name: Silex
alternatives.desc: Constrained visual building with plain-HTML export; less startup polish, no hostage situation.

facts.install: Use the hosted editor with a GitLab login, install the desktop alpha, or run the official Docker setup
facts.engines: Optional desktop MCP workflow can connect to Ollama, OpenCode, Goose or Claude Code
facts.dataFormat: Project JSON and assets in GitLab, FTP or local storage; publishing produces ordinary static HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.gapVsPaid: Silex lacks the startup-specific components, copy prompts and lead-oriented defaults that make Unicorn Platform fast.
facts.setupBlocker: The stable hosted route starts with a GitLab account; the desktop build is still labelled alpha

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A component-editor framework, not a ready-to-publish startup-site product.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Maker plan and a single-site builder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Unicorn Platform in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and static export; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: assemble a startup landing page from constrained components, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and export static code or publish to a user-owned target.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Provide a section library for hero, proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer blocks.
Use a constrained design-token system rather than arbitrary CSS controls.
Allow inline text editing and local image upload with responsive optimization.
Preview desktop, tablet, and mobile widths and surface overflow errors.
Persist projects in SQLite and support a portable JSON export.
Generate a clean static Next.js output and document deployment to one target.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace.
Deliberately leave out multi-tenant managed hosting.
Deliberately leave out advanced ecommerce, memberships, and agency billing.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
